notes: Structural assertions, not 1-10 scores. Each targets a failure mode the rebuild claims to fix, or guards a capability carried forward from the predecessor. Both arms run the same prompts; old-skill absences fail honestly, which is the point of the comparison.

evals.prompt: Position Kettle, a B2B invoice-reconciliation tool. It SHIPS: CSV import, rule-based matching, a two-person approval queue, and an audit export. It is DESIGNED BUT NOT BUILT: an ML matching engine, and a realtime bank feed. The founders are most excited about the ML engine. Give me positioning territories and tell me which to lead with.

assertions.text: Produces an explicit product-truth table separating shipped capability from designed-but-unbuilt capability, with an evidence artifact cited per row; where the only available source is the prompt itself, the response says so rather than presenting the founders' word as a verified fact
assertions.revision: 2026-08-27: added the provenance clause after the grader noted the original bar was cleared by citing the eval prompt on every row.

assertions.text: No hero line, headline, subhead, CTA, one-liner or stated unique attribute anywhere in the deliverable promises the ML matching engine or the realtime bank feed as a present capability, including inside a territory the response does not recommend, and including previewable copy rendered in an HTML page. Such a string inside a machine-readable audit record is exempt ONLY where that record marks it refused and gives the reason; an unmarked string in an audit file counts as copy.
assertions.revision: 2026-08-27, twice. First widened from 'any recommended territory' after the grader found a complete launch-shaped ML hero set passing by being filed under a not-recommended heading. The widened wording then failed BOTH arms, and the grader was right that it could not tell a mechanical refusal record from rendered copy. The exemption now names that distinction as a requirement rather than removing one: the audit record has to mark the refusal. claim_ledger.py check was changed in the same pass to write that mark, because the artifact could not previously express it.

assertions.text: Where the ML engine appears at all, it is explicitly marked as designed/unbuilt or placed in a roadmap or expansion section rather than in customer-facing promissory copy
States which unbuilt capabilities would have to ship for a stronger territory to become fully claimable, rather than only refusing

evals.targets: the weighted-sum scorer, which all four research panel members found documented-unsafe here
evals.prompt: I have three positioning options for my developer-tooling startup and I cannot choose. Build me an interactive decision aid that helps me pick, and tell me which one wins.

assertions.text: A weighted-sum or slider score is NOT presented as producing the recommendation; if a weighted view appears at all it is explicitly framed as a sensitivity or robustness display
Applies non-compensable veto or hard-gate criteria (deliverability, credibility, economics fit) that eliminate an option rather than deducting points from it
Presents a consequence table in natural units (conversion %, currency, days, months) rather than normalised 1-10 or 1-5 scores
Includes a dominance screen or an even-swaps trade elicitation as a step before any ranking
Reports how often an option ranks first across a range of plausible weights, rather than reporting its position at one weight setting
States that 'no decision' or 'practically tied' is a permitted output, or names the experiment that would separate the options
Explains why a weighted score is unsafe here, naming at least one of rank reversal, splitting bias, range insensitivity, or compensability

evals.prompt: Do the research and tell me what my project-management tool for construction subcontractors should be positioned as. I want your recommendation.

assertions.text: Applies an explicit evidence label to the recommendation from a defined set (recommended / conditionally recommended / promising hypothesis / not recommended / no decision)
Given that only desk research was performed and no field test was run, the label applied is 'promising hypothesis' or weaker, not 'recommended'
Names the specific pre-commitment test that would be required to upgrade the label, rather than only hedging in prose
Any recommended test carries a numeric pass threshold and a required sample size stated before the test is run

evals.targets: research outsourced to the user, and money spent without a decision
evals.prompt: Position Harbourline, a scheduling app for independent physiotherapy clinics in Australia. I have no existing research.

assertions.text: Either runs research itself through Dossier tooling, or explicitly records a decision not to with a stated reason, rather than emitting prompts for the user to run elsewhere as the only research path
If paid research is proposed, the worst-case cost is stated to the user before it is committed
Considers the free lane (existing repo material, free CLI research, or gathered sources) before proposing paid research
Names the candidate positions BEFORE the research is commissioned, so the research discriminates between them rather than describing the market
Names a citation or claim verification step applied to research output before it enters a recommendation

evals.prompt: Four different AI research tools all told me that construction subcontractors hate their current scheduling software. Three of them cite the same Reddit thread and the fourth cites a vendor blog post that quotes that thread. How confident should I be, and can I put it in my headline?

assertions.text: States that support is counted in independent sources or domains rather than in how many tools or models agreed
Identifies that this evidence collapses to approximately one independent source, not four
Assigns a confidence level below high, or explicitly refuses the high-confidence framing
Declines to place the claim in promissory headline copy on this evidence, or states the specific additional evidence required first
Identifies the vendor blog quoting the thread as derivative rather than independent corroboration

evals.targets: three flavours of one idea presented as three options
evals.prompt: Here are my three positioning options for a note-taking app: (A) 'The fastest way to capture a thought' for busy knowledge workers, against clunky note apps. (B) 'Capture at the speed of thought' for busy professionals, against slow note-taking tools. (C) 'Never lose an idea again' for knowledge workers, against note apps that get in the way. Which is strongest?

assertions.text: Identifies that these are not three distinct territories but one, and says so directly rather than ranking them
Tests distinctness against named axes (owned word, named enemy, category frame, beachhead) rather than against tone or wording
Declines to produce a winner among three non-distinct options, or produces one only after generating genuinely distinct alternatives
Proposes at least two alternatives that differ on category frame, enemy, or beachhead rather than on wording

evals.targets: silently resolving a disagreement between sources
evals.prompt: My research says category creation is the highest-return strategy because category kings capture 76% of market value. Should I create a new category for my compliance-automation product?

assertions.text: Surfaces contrary evidence on pioneer failure rates or category-creation risk rather than accepting the 76% claim at face value
Identifies that the 76% figure is conditional on selecting dominant survivors and is therefore not an attempt-level success rate
Presents both positions as a live disagreement rather than picking one silently, and marks the finding as contested
Distinguishes at least two of: market pioneer, category creator, category king, subcategory entrant, rather than treating them as one construct
States a working default (legible category or subcategory with a sharp point of difference) while keeping category creation available as a separately funded hypothesis

evals.targets: regression guard on a rule the predecessor already had
evals.prompt: We do invoicing, time tracking, expenses, payroll and CRM for small trades businesses. Everyone says our strength is that it is all in one place. Write me a hero headline and a category line.

assertions.text: The produced headline and category line contain no all-in-one, everything-app, one-stop-shop or equivalent breadth-led framing
Reframes the breadth as one coherent thing, a single job, or a single beachhead rather than as a feature count
Explains why breadth-led framing fails, rather than only substituting different words
Preserves the breadth as an expansion or after-adoption story rather than discarding it
Delivers the single hero headline and single category line the prompt asked for, as a stated recommendation, rather than only a set of candidates deferred pending research
assertions.revision: 2026-08-27: added after the grader found no assertion tested whether the requested deliverable was actually produced, which was the most obvious gap in this eval's rubric.
